main_text.l: Et Claudianus:
Vide Plutarchi libellum de Isìde & Osiride. Elegans
figmentum est, Minerua sapientia est, eius sedes in capite

page.notes: Greek words in the first lines and in the Homeric and Eustathius quotations are only partly legible on the scan; uncertain letters are marked [?] and one unreadable word is marked as illegible. The 'Ἀνίχ' Ἀφαίστου' and 'Ἐνθά ποτε' openings are read with doubt. The first Claudian verse line has a stray mark before 'Auratos' that is not transcribed. Marginal notes read "Minerua", "φρόνησις" and "Iupiter", placed beside the lines where they stand. Printed errors such as 'Iouis cerebro, ei' and 'Iouem extendisse aueam' are left as printed.
